name: FL-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: Wasserman Schultz's large financial advantage ($1.9M on hand vs ~$41K)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
Republican challenger is lightly funded and unknown
model.rationale: This is a heavily Democratic district where the incumbent holds a massive fundraising edge and markets price her near-certain to win; the Republican has raised only about $64,000. The seat stays safely Democratic despite the mid-cycle vacancy.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or an unexpectedly well-funded outside spending push for Andersen would be the main threat, but nothing in the evidence suggests one.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D) is running.

overview:
South Florida's 20th District is a solidly Democratic seat, and incumbent Debbie Wasserman Schultz is running to keep it after the mid-cycle resignation of the prior holder. She has raised over $3.3 million and holds $1.9 million on hand, dwarfing Republican Brent Andersen's roughly $64,000 in total fundraising and $41,000 in cash. Outside spending is modest and mostly favors her.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put her chances around 95 percent. With a D+20 partisan lean and no competitive evidence on the other side, the district remains safely Democratic, with the incumbent heavily favored in April 2026.
